start.text: The boat-stage is dressed stone, squared and fitted, with kerbs along both sides and a step down to the water green with weed. Keepers' work. At the end a stone bollard carries an iron mooring ring, worn bright on its seaward side where the same rope pulled on it, winter after winter.

On the bollard's cap somebody has scratched strokes in fives. Thirty winters of them, cut neat with a chisel point, the same hand as the lintel at the boat-watch up top. The last is fresher than the rest.
After them, smaller and rougher, scratched with a nail: strokes in fives, a lot of them. Not winters. Days.
After them, smaller and rougher, scratched with a nail: strokes in fives, days, and more of them every time you come down. Wenna's.
After them, smaller and rougher, scratched with a nail: strokes in fives, days, a long count of them. One line is drawn back through the whole count, end to end, hard.
The days stop. The last stroke has a line through it.

At the corner a timber post holds an iron bracket out over the water, and on its hook, where the boat's lantern went, hangs the Ridge Light's: gold behind horn, the only light on the shore that the fog gets out of the way of.
At the corner a timber post holds an iron bracket out over the water. Its hook is empty. That's where the boat's lantern went, you'd guess: the light the keeper climbed down to, once a winter.
Kindleby's skiff lies alongside, its line round the ring, pulling on the bright side.
